test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The first-ever night test match in India was played in Kolkata. What colour was the cricket ball used in the game?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pink**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The first-ever **Day-Night Test match** in India was played at the **Eden Gardens** stadium in **Kolkata** from **November 22 to 24, 2019**.
 
• The match featured the national teams of **India** and **Bangladesh**, serving as the second Test of the two-match series.
 
• A **Pink ball** was used for the game instead of the traditional red ball to ensure optimal **visibility** for players under **floodlights** during the evening and night sessions.
 
• The ball was manufactured by the Indian company **SG (Sanspareils Greenlands)**, featuring a **linen-based seam** and a brighter **fluorescent finish** to counteract the visibility issues caused by the twilight sky.
 
• India won the historic match by an **innings and 46 runs**, with **Ishant Sharma** becoming the first Indian bowler to take a five-wicket haul with the pink ball.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cricket Ball Varieties:**

 
 
• **Red Ball:** Used for standard **First-Class cricket** and traditional **Day Test matches**. It provides a sharp contrast against white kits but is hard to spot at night.
 
• **White Ball:** Specifically used in **One Day Internationals (ODIs)** and **T20 Internationals**. While highly visible under lights, it is not used in Test cricket as its color degrades significantly over 80 overs.
 
• **Yellow Ball:** This was briefly experimented with in early **night cricket** attempts in the late 1970s, but was ultimately rejected in favor of white and pink variations due to poor tracking against certain backgrounds.
